blocks.text: Business Associate agrees to:
2.1 Use and Disclosure Limitations. Not use or disclose PHI other than as permitted or required by this Agreement or as Required by Law.

blocks.text: 2.2 HITECH Direct Applicability. Recognize and comply with the fact that HITECH and its implementing regulations (including 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164, Subparts A, C, and D) apply directly to Business Associate in the same manner that such provisions apply to Covered Entity. Business Associate shall comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 C.F.R. §§ 164.308, 164.310, 164.312, and 164.316) with respect to ePHI.

blocks.text: 2.3 Safeguards. Use appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, and comply with the HIPAA Security Rule with respect to ePHI, to prevent use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided for by this Agreement.

runs.text: Use appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, and comply with the HIPAA Security Rule with respect to ePHI, to prevent use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided for by this Agreement.

blocks.text: 2.4 Reporting of Unauthorized Use or Disclosure. Report to Covered Entity, without unreasonable delay, any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this Agreement of which Business Associate becomes aware, including any Breaches of Unsecured PHI as required by 45 C.F.R. § 164.410 and any Security Incidents of which it becomes aware. In the case of a Breach of Unsecured PHI, Business Associate shall provide such notification to Covered Entity no later than thirty (30) calendar days after discovery of the Breach, and such notice shall include, to the extent possible, the information required under 45 C.F.R. § 164.410(c).

blocks.text: 2.5 Subcontractors. In accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.308(b)(2) and 164.502(e)(1)(ii), ensure that any Subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of Business Associate agree, by written contract, to the same restrictions, conditions, and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this Agreement with respect to such PHI.

blocks.text: 2.6 Access to PHI. To the extent Business Associate maintains PHI in a Designated Record Set, make such PHI available to Covered Entity (or, at Covered Entity’s direction, to an individual) to enable Covered Entity to fulfill its obligations to provide access to PHI under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.

blocks.text: 2.7 Amendment of PHI. To the extent Business Associate maintains PHI in a Designated Record Set, make such PHI available to Covered Entity for amendment, and incorporate any amendments to PHI as directed by or agreed to by Covered Entity pursuant to 45 C.F.R. § 164.526.

blocks.text: 2.8 Accounting of Disclosures. Maintain and make available to Covered Entity the information required to provide an accounting of disclosures of PHI as necessary to satisfy Covered Entity’s obligations under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528. Business Associate shall document disclosures of PHI for a period of at least six (6) years from the date of the disclosure, including: (a) the date of disclosure; (b) the name of the entity or person who received PHI, and if known, the address of such entity or person; (c) a brief description of PHI disclosed; and (d) a brief statement of the purpose of the disclosure.

blocks.text: 2.9 Internal Practices. Make available its internal practices, books, and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services ("Secretary") for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.

blocks.text: 2.14 Audit Rights. Upon reasonable advance written notice, and no more than once per calendar year absent a suspected Breach or Security Incident, Business Associate shall permit Covered Entity, or an independent auditor designated by Covered Entity, to inspect Business Associate's policies, procedures, and safeguards relevant to the protection of PHI under this Agreement, in order to verify Business Associate's compliance with this Agreement and the HIPAA Rules. Any such audit shall be conducted during normal business hours and shall not unreasonably interfere with Business Associate's operations.

blocks.text: ARTICLE V - TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 Term. This Agreement shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall continue in effect until all PHI provided by Covered Entity to Business Associate, or created or received by Business Associate on behalf of Covered Entity, is destroyed or returned to Covered Entity, or, if such return or destruction is infeasible, protections are extended in accordance with Section 5.4 below.

blocks.text: 5.2 Termination for Cause. Upon Covered Entity’s knowledge of a material breach or violation by Business Associate of this Agreement, Covered Entity shall: (a) provide written notice to Business Associate and give Business Associate an opportunity to cure the breach or end the violation within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of written notice; (b) immediately terminate this Agreement if Business Associate has breached a material term and cure is not possible; or (c) if termination is not feasible, report the breach to the Secretary in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.504(e)(1)(ii).

blocks.text: 5.3 Effect of Termination. Upon termination of this Agreement for any reason, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI received from Covered Entity or created or received by Business Associate on behalf of Covered Entity. Business Associate shall retain no copies of such PHI in any form. Business Associate shall certify in writing to Covered Entity that all PHI has been returned or destroyed within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination.

blocks.text: 5.4 Infeasibility of Return or Destruction. If Business Associate determines that returning or destroying PHI is infeasible, Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity in writing of the conditions that make return or destruction infeasible. In such event, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this Agreement to the PHI for as long as Business Associate retains the PHI, limit further uses and disclosures of PHI to those purposes that make return or destruction infeasible, and upon resolution of the conditions that make return or destruction infeasible, return or destroy the PHI.
